_comment: The Quests page, section by section.
WHY GO NEAR IT AT ALL. Fifteen quest ids are already referenced as gates by
the mines and the shops — `breaking_the_fire_seal`, `upgrade_the_inn` — and
until the quests exist those are dangling references that refint skips only
because the dataset is empty. A gate the app cannot name is a gate it cannot
explain.
DESCRIPTIONS ARE NEVER READ. Column two of every table on this page is the
quest's in-game text, verbatim, in the player character's voice. The
'Requirements to Complete' column is the wiki's own prose. Neither is
captured. What is: the name, the kind, who gives it, and the rewards — plus
delivery objectives where the wiki writes them as `{{ItemIcon|Heather}} (3)`,
which is a structured fact rather than a sentence.
NAME CELLS DIFFER BY SECTION, so the strategy is declared rather than
guessed:
id   — the name cell carries an `id="greetthetownsfolk"` anchor
link — the name is a wiki link ([[Adeline/Heart_Events#Four_Hearts|…]])
text — the name is the first plain-text cell that isn't just a row number
The Cooking and Mission tables open with a `#` column, which is why 'text'
skips purely numeric cells rather than taking the literal first one.
OBJECTIVES. `objectivesFromEnd` counts cells back from the last one, because
Rewards is always last and the columns before it are not consistent. Requests
and Cooking Challenges put a deliverable item there; Mission Quests put a
monster count, and monsters are not ingested, so it is left off rather than
recorded as an item that does not exist.
The page is stamped v0-14-1 and predates 1.0; every record says so.

ignoreSections.reason: the Request Board's location page, not a quest table
